answer: Judean date palm (Masada seed, germinated 2005, radiocarbon 155 BC–AD 64)
why: The Masada date seed is the oldest seed germinated with human help (it beat a ~1,300-year-old lotus seed). Older Silene stenophylla plants (2012) were regenerated from fruit tissue, not grown from a seed, so the card's answer holds.

answer: Beams of electromagnetic radiation from their magnetic poles
why: Pulsars are highly magnetised rotating neutron stars (not black-hole remnants) whose polar beams sweep past Earth like a lighthouse.
The card's statement (right to bear arms) is false; the WSPU suffragettes campaigned from 1903 for votes for women.
The statement 'Andromeda lies in the Milky Way' is false; Hubble's Cepheid observations of 1923–24 put it far outside, as a separate galaxy.

In September 2000 NASA announced that Chandra had 'clinched the case for a new type of black hole', an intermediate-mass black hole in M82. Hubble's intermediate-mass candidates came later (2002 onwards).
The statement (Odysseus) is false; Arrian and Plutarch tell of Alexander at Gordium in 333 BC.

Mangel (der/die Mangel) and Service (der/das Service) are each two Duden headwords told apart by their article. Zeit is one headword (it has several senses but no second word). why: The river with the longest course in Germany is the Rhine (865 km). It flows mainly south to north, so the statement 'flows west to east' is false. The Danube, which does flow west to east, is longer overall but has only 618–647 km in Germany. The body already explains this.

An autoclave sterilises with pressurised steam, typically at 121 °C, killing even spores. It was invented by Chamberland in 1879. The card's 'kills all forms of life' is a slight overstatement (prions resist standard cycles), but the open question is unaffected.
The statement (45.3 %) is false. The Sun holds 99.86 % of the solar system's mass (de.wikipedia); NASA rounds this to 99.8 %.

The statement (always below 40 °C) is false. The first official reading above 40 °C in Germany was 40.2 °C at Gärmersdorf on 27 July 1983. The body is already current: the national record is 41.8 °C at Drewitz, June 2026.
